key_insight: PercepCap makes video captioning more transparent by separating what the model perceives in space and time before it writes the final caption. This exposes perceptual evidence and helps pinpoint where captioning errors come from.
problem_solved: Existing multimodal models often generate video captions directly, which hides whether mistakes come from poor spatial understanding, temporal reasoning, or both. This makes spatiotemporal errors hard to diagnose and improve.
method: Introduces structured spatio-temporal perception to explicitly capture where objects are and when events happen in a video.
Uses perceptual evidence as an intermediate step before caption generation, rather than producing captions from raw video inputs alone.
Aims to surface intermediate reasoning signals so errors can be traced back to specific spatial or temporal perception failures.
impact: This approach can improve debugging, interpretability, and reliability of video captioning systems. For practitioners, it offers a clearer path to diagnose failures and build stronger multimodal models for fine-grained video understanding.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: video input -> spatial perception -> temporal perception -> caption generation
Side-by-side comparison of direct captioning vs. structured perceptual captioning
Spatial heatmap or bounding-box overlay showing object locations in frames
Timeline graphic showing event ordering and when key actions occur
paper_title: PercepCap: Video Captioner with Structured Spatio-Temporal Perception
paper_authors: Yifan Xu, Zihao Wang, Zhixiao Wang, Jiaming Zhang, Yichun Yang
